Log: 'Persisted HL7-sourced MedicationAdministration id=01a03fe7-edb2-74c9-84c1-abee07f9be1a ... (wasUpdate=false)'; DB recorded tracking_id 01a03fe7-ede6-7d7f-8762-f5b1746750b3 with SELECTION firings i-last-local-anesthetic and w-last-local-anesthetic-max-dose plus one DOSE firing. Then injected the correction: same order, same RXA-2 sub-id, 68 mL at 20:49Z. Log: same administration id with '(wasUpdate=true)'. A second positive on patient or2806b: a bupivacaine 0.5% administration first landed outside the case window (operation_id NULL, tracking_id NULL, no evaluation at all), then its correction inside the window was evaluated as an edit - the row was stamped tracking_id 01a03fea-ab31-7d38-ae7a-ecc6bea0ff4a and only the four DOSE rules were recorded (rule_not_fired_results), zero SELECTION rules.
evidence.negative: Injected a genuinely separate administration on the same order for patient or2806a: ORC-2=ORD2806A but RXA-2=2, 20 mL at 20:53Z. It was NOT treated as an edit - a second medication_administrations row was created (calculated 50 mg) under a new tracking id 01a03fe9-b748-79b4-b0c1-df50f339eeb9, and selection rules ran for it: three SELECTION firings including w-last-local-anesthetic-max-dose, whose LOCAL_ANESTHETIC_ADMINISTRATIONS detail listed both nerve blocks - [{"dose":"50 mg","time":"at 20:53"},{"dose":"170 mg","time":"at 20:49"}] - the same two-blocks-minutes-apart shape the ticket asks about, here correctly reported because there really were two.
evidence.red_check: Recompiled DefaultHL7ProcessingContext inside the running container with the fix's evaluator seam reverted to its pre-fix value (.edit(edit) -> .edit(false), which is what the parent commit passed unconditionally), lombok hand-expanded because lombok is absent from the runtime classpath. Backed up the eight shipped DefaultHL7ProcessingContext*.class files, installed the rebuilt ones into /app/classes, restarted the container (booted clean in 14.9s). Re-sent an edit for patient or2806b (same order/sub-id, 14 mL at 20:55Z): selection now ran for the correction - the previously absent log line 'Rule evaluated: w-indication-dose-options -> false No indication configurations found for medication: m-bupivacaine-0.5' appeared for the first and only time at 21:13:46.541Z, and two SELECTION firings (i-last-local-anesthetic, w-last-local-anesthetic-max-dose) were written under that administration's tracking id where the fixed build had written none. Re-sent an edit for patient or2806a too (70 mL at 20:57Z): it produced a DUPLICATE w-last-local-anesthetic-max-dose SELECTION firing at 21:14:23 under tracking id 01a03fe7-ede6..., re-scoring the corrected dose as a new selection. Restored the eight backed-up class files, confirmed all eight md5sums identical to the originals (28bdd62dd04d49276abfa57ee22bdc32 for the main class), restarted, and re-ran the positive: the edit at 21:15:06 produced only a DOSE firing and no SELECTION firing. The red-check log line still occurs exactly once in the whole captured log.

red_check_signature: No indication configurations found for medication: m-bupivacaine-0.5
caveats: The red check reverted the fix at its evaluator seam (.edit(edit) -> .edit(false)) rather than checking out the parent commit verbatim; the parent's DefaultHL7ProcessingContext no longer compiles against the current Request record, which dropped the orderId component.

Only the selection-suppression half of the change was shown to alter runtime behaviour. The dose-history exclusion (excludeAdminFromContextPatient by tracking id) produced identical cumulative numbers with and without the fix in this environment - the DOSE firing reported the same REMAINING_PERCENT 65% before and after - so the double-counting it guards against was not reproduced here.
The infusion edit path (editedInPlace in saveInfusionAdmin) and the MGB notification path that the same commit touched were not exercised.

Cases and patients were staged through the admin API rather than a real SIU case-create, and messages went through POST /api/admin/hl7-inbound-messages/send (the same processTenantMessage path as the live integration endpoint, minus apiTokenId).

automation.assessment: Unit coverage at the wiring boundary is already strong and was added with the fix: DefaultHL7ProcessingContextMedAdminEvaluationTest asserts edit vs non-edit for bolus and infusion, tracking-id carry-through, and stamping before the snapshot; EMRAdministeredMedicationProcessorEditExclusionTest asserts the exclusion and that an edit skips selection. All of it mocks the processor or the context patient at the boundary. What no test covers is the end-to-end consequence in the database: that a RAS correction of a bolus writes no second SELECTION rule execution result, while a new RXA-2 sub-id on the same order does. That is the observable a reviewer would check, and it is what this validation exercised by hand.
proposed_tests: Integration test: process a Mayo RAS bolus, then the same ORC-2 + RXA-2 sub-id with a changed dose and time, and assert one medication_administrations row plus exactly one SELECTION rule_fired_result under its tracking id.
Integration test: same order, new RXA-2 sub-id, and assert a second administration row with its own tracking id and its own SELECTION firings - the two-blocks-minutes-apart case from the ticket.
Integration test: a bolus that lands outside the case window (no operation, no tracking id) followed by a correction inside it, asserting the row gets a tracking id and is evaluated as an edit.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: A Mayo RAS correction of a bolus (same order and RXA-2 sub-id, changed dose and time) overwrote the administration in place and was evaluated as an edit, recording only a dose firing and no second selection firing for the corrected dose.
Negative: The same order with a new RXA-2 sub-id was treated as a separate administration, creating a second row with its own tracking id and its own selection firings, and the local anesthetic summary correctly listed both nerve blocks.
Red check: Reverting the evaluator seam to its pre-fix value and reinstalling the class in the running container made the same correction run selection rules again, producing a duplicate local-anesthetic max-dose firing; the class was restored and the checksums re-verified.

Automation: Unit coverage of the edit wiring already ships with the fix; proposed is an integration test that a RAS correction writes no second selection result while a new sub-id does.
